title: Fetches for element resources should use the response's "unsafe response" for network status and response bodies

labels.name: security/privacy
labels.description: There are security or privacy implications

body:
For a bit of background, see: https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/issues/1664

After using Fetch infrastructure to retrieve a resource, e.g. HTMLMediaElement's media resource, we should go through the response's unsafe response to inspect the network status of the response and read its body. When the response is CORS-cross-origin, Fetch will provide an [opaque filtered response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-filtered-response-opaque), which will always have a null body and network status of 0. The HTML spec fails to handle this case, thus all CORS-cross-origin responses will be dropped.

Over at [SerenityOS](https://github.com/SerenityOS/serenity), we've run into this issue for the following fetching elements so far:
* [HTMLMediaElement](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#loading-the-media-resource:body-incrementally-read)
* [HTMLImageElement](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/images.html#updating-the-image-data:concept-fetch)
* [HTMLLinkElement](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element:concept-fetch)

Note that [HTMLScriptElement does actually handle this already](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#fetching-scripts:unsafe-response-2) by inspecting the unsafe response.
